scope: geistlib#286: early exit as the default of geistr decide --escalate chat. The declaration is geistlib's; this is a frozen copy of it, and the contract block restates its numbers for the verifier.

contract.early_exit_rule: the first probe at position >= probe_interval whose top softmax probability over the options (temperature 1) is >= tau answers with its argmax; without one, the full-reasoning answer
contract.full_rule: stop eos: the scored answer; a capped answer without a final letter is wrong
contract.primary: paired gain/loss exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) intervals, Bonferroni joint coverage: non-inferior iff lower >= -margin_pp

declared.decided_by: user (2026-10-29: #286 approved; declare by PR before any inference, night-only)
declared.question: Is early exit (tau 0.8, probes every 128 tokens, frozen in #236) non-inferior to full reasoning at cap 8192 on Bonsai 2 27B, within the 2 pp margin, so that it can become the default of decision mode?

sample.population: the cleaned classic-MMLU test split (13,904; cais/mmlu c30699e8, exact-overlap exclusion) minus the 500 #171/#236 test questions (cases-test/test.jsonl sha256 108f815e3c21f6fe17adc4fa25d5a14f3051473349e156c06f59f46f86aa3977): 13,404
sample.policy: decision_dataset.select_stratified (subject-proportional largest-remainder quotas, 21-386 per subject over 57 subjects; within a subject the first by sha256([seed, question_id]); label-independent)
sample.question_ids_sha256_of: the selected question_ids in selection order, joined by newlines
sample.prepare: tools/prepare_decision_eval.py --splits test --test-sample 3500 --test-seed geist-decision-test-sample-286-v1 --test-exclude <#171 cases-test/test.jsonl>, otherwise the #171 frozen prompt policy (5 shots, exclude, rotations 1, template date 2026-10-04)

sample_size.rule: decision_metrics.paired_quality (exact binomial gain/loss intervals, Bonferroni), 2 pp margin, at the #236 cap-8192 discordance (27 gains, 27 losses in 500: 5.4 % each)
sample_size.note: n = 3,500 establishes the margin at that discordance if the true difference is above about -0.2 pp (at -0.25 pp the bound is -2.02).

run.settings: Bonsai 2 27B PQ2_0 (3907dc16...), Metal on the M1 Max, FP32 KV, 6 threads, OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive, greedy, chat_reasoning prompts in subject order, per-subject prefix snapshot aligned to 320, cap 8192, batch 8 refilled as questions finish (no --pad), probes [198, 248069, 271] every 128 generated tokens recorded with --exit-tau 0
run.both_arms_from_one_run: Probes are transparent (#236 step 1: 8/8 generations token-identical with and without probes), so the recorded run is the full-reasoning arm. The early-exit arm is the frozen policy applied to the recorded probes of the same generation: the first probe at position >= 128 whose top softmax probability over the four options (temperature 1) is >= 0.8 answers with that option; without one, the full-reasoning answer. A question's two arms share one trajectory.
run.batching: Refilled batching without padding is sound here: both arms of a question come from the same generation, so which questions share its batched steps (and the per-n rounding of those steps) cannot favour either arm. Padding was needed in #236 only because the arms were separate runs. A question in flight at a chunk deadline is re-run from its prompt in the next chunk; finished questions are never re-run.
run.scoring: eval_decision.generation_outcome, thinking on, as in #171/#236; a capped full answer without a final letter is wrong for the full arm

analysis.primary: paired_quality(early exit, full reasoning, margin 2 pp): non-inferior iff the lower bound of the conservative 95 % interval is above -2 pp
analysis.secondary: accuracy of both arms, gains/losses, early exits, capped answers, generated tokens and their ratio, probe count and time; results file + JSON by PR
analysis.no_interim: No interim analysis: the 3,500 are analysed once, after all are complete (progress reports give counts and throughput only, no accuracy).

latency_check.questions: 300 of the 3,500: decision_dataset.select_stratified(the 3,500, 300, seed geist-decision-latency-286-v1), question_ids_sha256 0afb9f8a4dad53ea3f485f5d660fd75f357859dde820fa4c8addabedf0306717
latency_check.when: after the main run is complete
latency_check.run: live early exit with the decision-mode defaults (probe every 128, tau 0.8), same settings, batch 8 refilled, no padding
latency_check.method_note: geistr decide --early-exit (geist-runtime #256) runs the same probe sequence (snapshot, prefill the thinking close, read the option logits, restore) between geistr_chats_next steps. The engine driver runs it here because it takes the prepared MMLU prompts; geistr decide builds its own prompt, whose answers could not be compared with the offline arm.
latency_check.reported: p50/p95 per-question latency (prompt to answer, including its prefill) and aggregate generated tokens/s for live early exit; the same for full reasoning on the same 300 from the main run (also with its probe time subtracted); agreement of the live answers with the offline early-exit answers (reported, not required to be identical: different batch companions round differently)

declared.schedule: night-only, 21:00-07:00 Berlin: a scheduler starts chunks only inside the window and stops starting new ones at 07:00; chunks under 28-min wall-clock deadlines, LOCK_PRIO=batch, LOCK_MAX=30, cool start, caffeinate, resumable from frozen manifests
declared.estimate: full reasoning about 1,350 tokens per question (#236 cap 8192): about 4.7 M tokens at about 50-58 tok/s aggregate with 8 in flight, plus about 37,000 probes at about 0.12 s and prefix prefills: about 25-27 h of lease; latency check about 1 h; about 4 nights at about 7 h of lease per night
declared.if_noninferior: a geist-runtime PR that makes --early-exit the default of geistr decide --escalate chat, left for the user's merge decision

amendments.decided_by: coordinator relay of the power-gate finding (#286 comment, PR #321): latency needs AC with Low Power Mode off
amendments.declared_before_inference: for the latency phase: yes (it has not started); the main run is in progress and unchanged
amendments.reason: The M1 Max was found on battery with Low Power Mode on (2026-10-30), which slows Mac timings by about 1.5x. pmset -g log shows AC vs battery but not Low Power Mode, so the main run's per-question latencies (night 1: AC except about 3 min of chunk 0; Low Power Mode unknown) cannot serve as the verified full-reasoning reference of the latency check.
amendments.power_gate: Every latency-phase chunk starts only on AC with Low Power Mode off (campaign.sh waits without holding the lock; run.sh re-checks under the lock). Power state is sampled every 30 s during every chunk (power-<job>.log). A latency chunk with any sample off AC or with Low Power Mode on is discarded and its questions re-run.
amendments.latency_check_change: Both latency arms are measured live under the gate on the same 300 questions: early exit (tau 0.8, as declared) and full reasoning (tau 0, probes recorded, as in the main run), in that order. The comparison uses these two runs; the main run's latencies for the 300 are reported for reference only. Agreement of the live early-exit answers with the offline early-exit answers stays as declared.
amendments.estimate: about 2.5-3 h of extra lease for the full-reasoning arm of the 300
amendments.unchanged: sample, main run, primary analysis, accuracy evidence (power does not change the computation, only its speed)
